lines.en: label christmastwo17:
scene norikospresent1
Somehow, I wind up in front of Noriko.
She holds a box that is both familiar and unfamiliar at the same time- which I’m sure sounds strange to you, but there’s no other way I can think of describing it.
I’m assuming this is that present she was telling me about a while back.
I still have no idea what to expect but, having grown to know this girl relatively well over the last several months, it’s safe to assume it’s likely something with some sort of...sentimental value.
Despite her appearance, Noriko’s consistently been one of the most sentimental people I know.
And I see no reason for her to break that pattern now- on a night that I’m sure she wishes she could have enjoyed with me in a different sort of way.
Perhaps in the future, if there even is one.
: Heeeeeey...
: I went up to the hotel room to find you, but Makoto told me you were busy with Miku, so...I figured I’d just wait around in the lobby until you showed up.
: Did she like her present?
: Yes and no. It’s a little complicated.
scene norikospresent2
: Yeah...I can...definitely relate to that.
: I take it that’s for me, then?
: Yeah...
: Am I allowed to open it?
scene norikospresent3
: Huh? Yeah. Why wouldn’t you be?
: I’m just getting mixed signals between you and the box itself and I’m currently choosing sides.
: Well...I guess I should be pretty nervous then, huh?
: Probably not. I can’t imagine myself ever choosing a box over you.
scene norikospresent4
: Yeah...we’ll see about that...
: Give it here, then. There’s no better place to break the rules than a hotel lobby and I am now determined to go against that box’s wishes.
: You know it wasn’t the box who wrote “Do not open” on itself, right?
: Also, can we maybe, like...not do this in here? I’d like to be somewhere a little more private since I’m probably going to cry.
: I don’t know if I like the idea of whatever this present is making you cry, but if going somewhere else is what it takes for me to figure it out, sure.
: I’m assuming Kirin told you about the boiler room, then?
scene norikospresent3
: Boiler room? What are you talking about?
: Oh. Nevermind. I just figured that’s what you meant with the whole “privacy” thing.
: I’m mostly under the impression by now that Kirin just tells you everything immediately after it happens and-
: What were you and Kirin doing in-
scene norikospresent5
: Actually...no. That’s not important right now. I’ve only got a little while until I have to head back and...I kinda need you to see this before that.
: You’re leaving already? Why?
scene norikospresent6
: I don’t want to leave.
: I just think I’ll have a harder time staying around after you see what’s inside the box.
: Um...anyway...
: I’m pretty sure the roof is unlocked...and it’s not that cold out tonight, so we can probably do this up there?
: Stairs and boxes, my two favorite things.
: Lead the way. I’ll be right behind you.
: Not for long, you won’t.
scene black
I’m not exactly sure what Noriko means by that, but I follow her regardless.
And, of course, she’s the type of person to take the stairs instead of the elevator.
So on top of having to ascend what feels like an ungodly amount of stories, I have to deal with the exhaustion of actually moving now as well.
But if this is what it takes for her to cry in a contained environment rather than one that a classmate could pop into at any given moment, I guess it’s just something I have to deal with.
scene clearnightsky
As we open the door and step out onto the roof, I wonder how many more girls I’ll be forced to watch cry before the night comes to an end.
So much for Christmas being the most magical night of the year- if that’s even a thing people say.
But I guess that crying in itself is sort of magical in a way.
Not everyone is in tune enough with their feelings to do something like that. And many of the people who are would just...rather not.
I’d say I hate it myself, but it’s been so long at this point that I don’t know if I can even attribute such a strong word to the idea of tears.
I will say with utmost certainty, though, that it’s a lot harder to hate something when you’re only experiencing it secondhand.
The two of us approach the edge of the hotel and sit down on the concrete rooftop.
It’s cold. Much colder than the air itself.
And despite being face to face with a girl prepared to be wounded all for the sake of tightening the rope wrapped around us-
All I can think of is wanting to go back inside.
scene norikospresent7
The box sits in my lap the same way she would when she was younger.
That’s not a memory, just an educated guess based on all that I’ve heard from her.
I’m sure she’s thinking something similar right now.
: So...how was the Christmas party without me being around? Any...I don’t know, quieter?
: Is this the part where you start stalling because you’re worried about how things are going to play out?
scene norikospresent8
: Ugh. I really should have tried rationing out all the times I’ve done that. I could seriously benefit from that tactic right now if you weren’t already familiar with my tricks.
: Guess you’re going to have to come up with a new method if you want some additional time in the future.
: Or not, since the world is just going to repeat itself soon anyway.
scene norikospresent9
: What, are we in some kind of movie right now?
: You gonna tell me that the only reason you don’t remember me is because you went all Eternal Sunshine on yourself?
: I have no idea what that is.
: Well, we should watch it together if you still want to be around me after tonight.

: Noriko, I’m not going to find the severed head of someone I care about inside of this box, am I? Because you seem really worried that whatever is in here is going to make me...dislike you or something.
: What if it was a severed head of someone you didn’t like? Then what?
: You’re stalling again and I’m not falling for it.
: You can’t fault me for trying.
: Can I open this now, then? Or do you know some spiritual hack where opening boxes facing west is somehow a good luck charm?
: You can open it.
: You’ve waited long enough.
scene norikospresent10
I peel back the tape covering the box and place it on the concrete.
The wind sweeps it away and carries it off the ledge immediately.
There’s some sort of metaphor or symbolism to be gleaned from that, but I can’t be bothered to decode it right now.
There’s nothing lavish or exciting inside of the box-
Just a stack of what appear to be organized papers with neat, half-cursive handwriting covering them.
I’m assuming that whatever the present is lies within these pages.
scene norikospresent11
: What is this?
scene norikospresent12
: Your past.
: Or a little piece of it at least.
: We’d need a lot more boxes to pack up our entire history.
: Did you write these?
: No.
scene nikil1
: Nee-chan wrote all of these for you after you disappeared.
: There were hundreds of them.
: She must have been writing one every single day for...I don’t even know how long.
: But obviously, she had no idea where to send them.
scene nikil2
: Not at first, at least.
: And even when you started seeing me again, it’s not like I could have just...delivered these to you.
: Like...I had no idea they even existed until I was going through her closet the other day.
: And if Nee-chan knew in the beginning that I was getting to spend time with you but not her, it would have broken her even more.
scene nikil3
: She loved you...so, so, so, so much.
: More than I ever did. More than I ever could.
: How can I compete with that, Sensei?
: I spent so much time psyching myself up and trying to win your affection like it was some sort of...contest that I lost sight of how I started with the biggest handicap of all.
: I’ve been second place forever. In everything.
: And if it wasn’t with Nee-chan, it was with Maya.
scene nikil4
: I’m just the...younger, spunkier version of the girl you used to love. And she’s still the same person she’s always been. So like...what's the point of me?
: Even if I’ve changed...even if the...perfect girl I dreamt up for you is completely to your liking...I still don’t have what she did.
: I don’t have that history.
: The...backlog of emotions and kisses and whatever other shit you guys did to each other before I even understood grammar.
: I couldn’t keep hiding this from you.
scene nikil5
: I mean...I could have kept hiding it from you. And it probably would have made my chances a million times better...
: But that wouldn’t be fair. To you...or Nee-chan...or even me in a sort of really roundabout way that I can probably justify if you give me enough time.
: So...yeah.
: If you can’t remember the past, I’ll bring the past to you.
: Even if it’s not my place to do that.
: Even if I have to steal embarrassing stuff out of my older sister’s closet because, at least until today, she was too stubborn to even think about telling you.
scene norikospresent13
: That wasn’t the last one, you know.
: There were tons more after that.
: Even when my parents were getting on her case about how it was becoming an unhealthy obsession...she never stopped.
: She never stopped loving you.
: And she never will.
scene norikospresent14
: Ugh. Right on cue. I told you I was going to cry.
: If your memories really are gone, I’m sure you might believe that these could just be fake or something...
: And I have no way of proving they’re not.
: But, no matter what you choose to believe or...what you decide to do from here on out...I think you should at least consider Nee-chan’s feelings.
: Mine too, if you can...but...
: Alas...
: Second place forever...
scene norikospresent15
: Sensei?
scene black
scene smile

scene norikospresent18
: Shouldn’t we be watching Christmas movies right now?
: It feels kind of weird to be watching anime when we told your parents we were going to do our own Christmas stuff instead of what they wanted to do.
: Are you kidding? Why would we watch something that lame when the newest episode of Gunfighter Z: Machine War Paradox Chronicles comes out tonight?
: Why are anime titles always so long? I don’t get it.
scene norikospresent19
: Well, you’re more than welcome to go back downstairs and play with Noriko instead if you want. Since you’re too much of a loser to watch giant robots blow up other giant robots, I mean.
: No thanks. She keeps trying to sit on my lap and it’s weird.
scene norikospresent20
: I know, right?! She thinks you’re like, her actual big brother or something. And my parents see no problem with it at all.
: I don’t think there’s a problem with it, I’d just rather hang out with you.
scene norikospresent21
: W-Well of course you’d rather hang out with me than some kid. That’s barely even a compliment.
: Then why are you blushing so much?
scene norikospresent22
: I...I’m not blushing! It’s just hot in my stupid room because my parents won’t turn the stupid heat off!
: Don’t you have a thermostat in here? Just turn it down yourself if you’re hot.
: Yeah, but...I don’t know how to use it...
: You’re completely helpless, aren’t you?
: If you’re so smart, why don’t you do it?!
: Because you’re not actually hot. You’re just saying that.
: Why would I lie?! Also, shut up! Gunfighter is about to come on!
scene norikospresent23
: I’ll just turn the heat down myself.
: Even if your parents would get mad at you for doing it, they-
scene norikospresent24
: [[REDACTED]? What’s wrong?
: Nothing.
: I’m fine.
: I’m actually feeling a little cold, though...so I don’t think I’m going to turn the heat down after all.
: Cold? Oooooh...maybe there’s a ghost in the room?
: Yeah...maybe...
: [[REDACTED], no. I was obviously kidding. There’s no such thing as ghosts. They’re-
: You’re such a good boy.
scene norikospresent25
: It’s no wonder I fell in love with you.
: You try so hard to keep this side of you away from everyone that when it finally comes out, you just seem a million times cuter.
: You know, the best part about being in second place is that even if I don’t win, I always have a really clear view of the goal.
: I’ll keep running, Sensei. Forever and ever. Even when I know I can’t win.
: Even when my legs give out.
: And, who knows? Maybe the next obstacle I put down will wind up knocking someone else over instead of me.
scene norikospresent26
: Merry Christmas.
: Maybe next year I’ll get you a present that doesn’t immediately make me cry.
: I remembered something...
: Was it nice?
: I bet it was.
scene clearnightsky
My phone suddenly goes off in my pocket.
: Looks like my time here is up...
: You better answer that, Sensei.
: I bet it’s someone really important.
Noriko leaves the roof and I struggle to regain enough control of my hands to reach for my phone.
I look down at one of the letters and notice that I’ve been gripping it so tightly that it’s begun to crinkle and tear.
I can still see it- the vision of an old bedroom.
The scent of baked goods leaking in through the crack under the door and the feeling of my dick going numb from having to lie on it for so long to conceal an erection.
I can still imagine her face and the hue of her cheeks when I called her out for blushing.
But why that night?
Why would I recall something so small and insignificant when I’m sure there were thousands of other memories I made with her that were ten times bigger?
I don’t know.
I don’t know anything other than the fact that it’s true now. That Niki is who she says she is.
And so is Noriko, even if her new fascination is taking over the role of a martyr in an effort to get me back together with someone who she both loves and loathes all at once.
My phone goes off again.
I place the letter back inside of the box, closing it tightly and subconsciously reaching for the tape that had been carried off the ledge just moments ago.
Of course, I grasp nothing but the air itself.
But then-
I recover enough control to gaze into a small, electric rectangle and see who the cause of these beeps has been.
: Come downstairs right now. I know you’re up there. I need to talk to you. It’s important. Please.
: I’ll be in front of your hotel. Noriko gave me the address. And come alone. Don’t bring her. Please.
